name: Hericium erinaceus

ecology.substrate: wounds on old beech and oak

size_cm.note: fruit body 8 to 24 cm across; spines 1 to 4 cm long; North American collections

notes: A slow heart rot with a tooth-cushion fruit body. Reported (unchecked) to be cultivated and to have a sequenced genome.

tip_speed.source: Lu, Liu, Ren, Hu, Wang, Ji, Wang, Du, Liu, Yang & Yu 2024, Optimization of substrate formulation for Hericium erinaceus by replacing wood by straw and their effect on enzyme activities, Frontiers in Plant Science 15:1436385
tip_speed.note: strain 20190111, growth rate 4.92 mm/day (x 41.7 = 205 um/h); plate tests in that paper were at 25 C in the dark, and its wood-chip control substrate gave 4.43 mm/day. The paper mixes mm/d and cm/d labels; mm/d is used here

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Imtiaj, Jayasinghe, Lee, Shim, Rho, Lee, Hur, Lee, Lee & Lee 2008, Vegetative growth of four strains of Hericium erinaceus collected from different habitats, Mycobiology 36(2):88-92
t_opt.note: four strains (Korea, Japan, China) on PDA at pH 6, 15 to 35 C in 5 C steps, 10 days; best at 25 C, good from 20 to 30 C

t_max.note: growth was lowest and sometimes absent at 15 and 35 C (Imtiaj et al. 2008, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3755240/); 35 C taken as the upper limit. The lower limit was not reached in that study and is left at the family default

cold_drop.note: cultivation practice in Lu et al. 2024 (https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpls.2024.1436385/full): bags colonised at 25 C, fruited at 15 to 18 C; 25 minus the 16.5 C midpoint
